# render-across-releases.golden.txt — how this project's rendered output has
# moved since the previous release.
#
# Generated by tests/render_across_releases_test.go. Regenerate with:
#
#     go test ./tests -run TestRenderedOutputAcrossReleases -regenerate-goldens
#
# WHAT IT IS FOR. v0.4.0 changed table layout and v0.4.1 changed the edges footer
# and the chips, with every claim locked and byte-identical, the lock store
# untouched and `dossierx check` reporting nothing. A consumer's own merge gate
# cannot detect that for them; only a comparison against the release tag can.
#
# SILENT RENDER CHANGES is the section that matters: an artifact whose inputs did
# not move by a byte and whose rendered output did. Every entry there needs a
# CHANGELOG line, and the diff printed under it is what that line is written from.
#
# EXPLAINED BY AN INPUT CHANGE carries THE SAME DIFF, and the inputs that moved.
# The two sections differ in what they oblige you to do, never in what they show
# you. A fixture project's inputs are every tracked non-artifact file under it —
# nothing here knows which claim fed which line of a ten-thousand-line viewer —
# so one edited byte anywhere in a fixture moves that whole fixture's viewer into
# this section. If the section could suppress the diff, that one byte would also
# hide a renamed CSS class in the same viewer, which is precisely the v0.4.1
# change. So: read this section's diffs, and satisfy yourself that every hunk in
# them is accounted for by the named inputs. A hunk that is not is a silent
# render change wearing an explanation.
#
# THE BASELINE LINE IS PART OF THE SNAPSHOT. It records which release this was
# compared against, so the comparison is auditable rather than implied. The
# baseline defaults to the newest tag reachable from HEAD; DOSSIERX_PREV_RELEASE_TAG
# overrides it, and an override that names a different release must be
# regenerated, because a report whose header says one release and whose diffs
# describe another would be worse than no report. Regenerating after a tag is a
# release step, in the same breath as regenerating surface.json.
#
# An empty report is the expected steady state immediately after a release.

baseline   v0.7.5 (fe2c61375d62985c7f0e0a07ec39293af822f835)
compared   148 rendered artifacts present at both revisions
added      4
removed    0
silent     3 rendered differently from byte-identical inputs
explained  0 rendered differently after their own inputs changed

+   COLOUR MECHANISM, in cascade order. shell.html emits three <style> blocks:
+   graph.css, then this file, then the generated theme block.

+   1. One unconditional `:root` holds the palette, and it is LIGHT-FIRST:
+      every value in it is both the light-OS value and the printed value.
+      There is exactly one such block in this file.
+   2. `@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` re-points the handful
+      of tokens that invert. The `screen and` prefix is load-bearing: it is
+      what keeps a dark-mode OS from dragging dark ink onto paper.
+   3. The single `@media print` block is the LAST block in this file. It has
+      to be last, because it overrides screen layout rules at equal
+      specificity (`.content-area { padding: 0 }` beats the padded screen
+      rule only on source order), and it pins `color-scheme: light`.
+   4. internal/render appends the project's theme as the third <style>: an
+      optional @font-face run, a shared `:root`, then
+      `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light), print` and
+      `@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`. The project's light
+      block deliberately also matches `print` and its dark block deliberately
+      cannot, so a token a project sets only under `dark:` prints the engine's
+      light value rather than its dark one.
+
+   The names a project may set are the 28-entry allowlist in
+   internal/config/config.go (ThemeTokenAllowlist). Each token's :root default
+   is the value a light OS gets, and the screen-dark block carries the dark
+   values for the three that differ. A consumer spells the token as
+   `var(--token, <fallback>)`; the fallback is the LIGHT value, because this
+   sheet is light-first and because the fallback only ever fires for a
+   viewer.template_overrides project that forked this file and dropped the
+   :root — which should degrade to light, not to dark.
+
+   A token has to be read by the declaration that WINS, not merely by a
+   declaration. Two rules in this file are re-declared later at equal
+   specificity (`code` and the fenced-block list `.claim-body pre,
+   .claim-list-items pre, .sbody pre, .comment-body pre, .claim-tree-body`),

+   COLOUR MECHANISM, in cascade order. shell.html emits three <style> blocks:
+   graph.css, then this file, then the generated theme block.

+   1. One unconditional `:root` holds the palette, and it is LIGHT-FIRST:
+      every value in it is both the light-OS value and the printed value.
+      There is exactly one such block in this file.
+   2. `@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` re-points the handful
+      of tokens that invert. The `screen and` prefix is load-bearing: it is
+      what keeps a dark-mode OS from dragging dark ink onto paper.

+      rule only on source order), and it pins `color-scheme: light`.
+   4. internal/render appends the project's theme as the third <style>: an
+      optional @font-face run, a shared `:root`, then
+      `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light), print` and
+      `@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`. The project's light
+      block deliberately also matches `print` and its dark block deliberately
+      cannot, so a token a project sets only under `dark:` prints the engine's
+      light value rather than its dark one.
+
+   The names a project may set are the 28-entry allowlist in
+   internal/config/config.go (ThemeTokenAllowlist). Each token's :root default
+   is the value a light OS gets, and the screen-dark block carries the dark
+   values for the three that differ. A consumer spells the token as
+   `var(--token, <fallback>)`; the fallback is the LIGHT value, because this
+   sheet is light-first and because the fallback only ever fires for a
+   viewer.template_overrides project that forked this file and dropped the
+   :root — which should degrade to light, not to dark.
+
+   A token has to be read by the declaration that WINS, not merely by a
+   declaration. Two rules in this file are re-declared later at equal
+   specificity (`code` and the fenced-block list `.claim-body pre,
+   .claim-list-items pre, .sbody pre, .comment-body pre, .claim-tree-body`),
+   so their token reads live in the later copy; internal/render/theme_tokens_test.go
+   asserts, per token, that the last declaration of the consumer's
+   selector+property pair is the one carrying the var(). It also fails if an
+   allowlisted token has no consumer in this file or in graph.css, and pins
+   the structural invariants listed above.
+
+   graph.css keeps the OPPOSITE convention for its own --dxg-* ramp (dark
+   base, light override) and says so in its own header; the two files differ
+   deliberately. */
+
+/* THE palette. One unconditional :root, light-first: the values below are what
+   a light-OS screen and a printed page both get. Nothing else in this file
+   declares any of these properties, so this block's position is free; it sits
+   here, at the top, because that is where a reader looks for it.
+
+   The dark query is scoped to `screen` on purpose. Without the prefix, a
+   reader whose OS is in dark mode and who hits Print gets near-black --paper
+   and pale --ink; print media does not carry an appearance, so nothing else
+   would put the light palette back. `screen and` is the whole fix, and the
+   @media print block at the end of the file pins `color-scheme: light` beside
+   it so form controls and scrollbars agree. This is unverified for Firefox and
+   Safari; where a browser already forces light for print it is a no-op, so it
+   is safe either way. */

-/* ---- print -------------------------------------------------------------
-   The first and only @media print block in this stylesheet. It exists for
-   one reason (Q4): paper has no disclosure widget, so a printed viewer that
-   honoured the collapsed <details> would silently drop every claim's
-   governed_by/rests_on/implemented-in footer — the exact facts a reviewer
-   prints the page to read.
-   Revealing the contents through CSS is deliberate rather than setting `open`,
-   which CSS cannot do: `open` is a content attribute, not a property a rule
-   can write.
-   Same mechanism, and the same two-rule pairing, as the .claim:target rule
-   above: a closed <details> hides its contents through the UA's
-   ::details-content pseudo-element, so that is what is targeted, and the
-   child-selector form is expected to be a no-op wherever the pseudo-element is
-   implemented. It is kept only as a fallback for engines that predate
-   ::details-content (Chrome/Edge 131+, Safari 18.4+, Firefox 139+) and hide
-   the contents some other way; such an engine drops the pseudo-element rule
-   and still prints as it did before v0.4.1. Both rules declare the same value
-   and carry equal specificity (0,1,2), so the pseudo-element rule is written
-   LAST — source order is the only thing ranking them.
-   This block is independent of the .claim:target rule, of the two
-   server-written `open` signals, and of the expand-all toolbar — whichever of
-   those is or is not in effect on screen, print shows all four states
-   identically.
-   SCOPE — stated plainly so the next reader knows this is a decision, not an
-   oversight: only the facet currently ON SCREEN prints. A collapsed footer
-   belonging to a claim in a facet group the reader is not looking at stays
-   unrendered, because its ancestor section.claim-group carries the `hidden`
-   attribute (computed display: none) and no rule here un-hides it. The rules
-   below reveal a disclosure inside a subtree that is being laid out; they
-   cannot resurrect a subtree that display: none removed from the box tree in
-   the first place. That is deliberate: printing a tabbed viewer has always
-   shown one facet, what v0.4.1 changes is that the shown facet's footers now
-   print with it, and un-hiding every facet for print is a larger design
-   change — page order, per-facet headings, the duplicated overview copies —
-   than a patch release should make.
-   Only the disclosure is touched. Nothing here restyles the card, the type
-   scale or the color tokens; a full print stylesheet is out of scope for
-   v0.4.1. */

+/* ---- print — THE @media print block ------------------------------------
+   There is exactly one @media print block in this stylesheet and this is it;
+   internal/render/theme_tokens_test.go fails if a second one appears.
+
+   IT MUST STAY LAST IN THE FILE. Several of the rules below beat a screen
+   rule of identical specificity purely on source order — `.content-area
+   { padding: 0 }` against the padded `.content-area` rule in the System
+   Record layer, `.system-record-head { padding-top: 0 }` against that layer's
+   `.system-record-head`. Move this block earlier and the printed page silently
+   regains the sidebar gutter.
+
+   color-scheme is pinned to light here to match the palette: the :root at the
+   top of the file is light-first and its dark query is `screen`-scoped, so
+   print already gets light custom properties; this line makes the UA-painted
+   parts (form controls, scrollbars, canvas) agree. Unverified for Firefox and
+   Safari; where a browser already forces light for print it is a no-op, so it
+   is safe either way.
+
+   Consolidated from three separate @media print blocks. Their reasons follow,
+   unchanged, one per group.
+
+   NOTE (Q4): paper has no button to press, so the source-note clamp must not
+   reach it — print shows every note whole and hides the control.
+
+   DISCLOSURE (Q4). Paper has no disclosure widget, so a printed viewer that
+   honoured the collapsed <details> would silently drop every claim's
+   governed_by/rests_on/implemented-in footer — the exact facts a reviewer
+   prints the page to read.
+   Revealing the contents through CSS is deliberate rather than setting `open`,
+   which CSS cannot do: `open` is a content attribute, not a property a rule
+   can write.
+   Same mechanism, and the same two-rule pairing, as the .claim:target rule
+   above: a closed <details> hides its contents through the UA's
+   ::details-content pseudo-element, so that is what is targeted, and the
+   child-selector form is expected to be a no-op wherever the pseudo-element is
+   implemented. It is kept only as a fallback for engines that predate
+   ::details-content (Chrome/Edge 131+, Safari 18.4+, Firefox 139+) and hide
+   the contents some other way; such an engine drops the pseudo-element rule
+   and still prints as it did before v0.4.1. Both rules declare the same value
+   and carry equal specificity (0,1,2), so the pseudo-element rule is written
+   LAST — source order is the only thing ranking them.
+   This block is independent of the .claim:target rule, of the two
+   server-written `open` signals, and of the expand-all toolbar — whichever of
+   those is or is not in effect on screen, print shows all four states
+   identically.
+   SCOPE — stated plainly so the next reader knows this is a decision, not an
+   oversight: only the facet currently ON SCREEN prints. A collapsed footer
+   belonging to a claim in a facet group the reader is not looking at stays
+   unrendered, because its ancestor section.claim-group carries the `hidden`
+   attribute (computed display: none) and no rule here un-hides it. The rules
+   below reveal a disclosure inside a subtree that is being laid out; they
+   cannot resurrect a subtree that display: none removed from the box tree in
+   the first place. That is deliberate: printing a tabbed viewer has always
+   shown one facet, what v0.4.1 changes is that the shown facet's footers now
+   print with it, and un-hiding every facet for print is a larger design
+   change — page order, per-facet headings, the duplicated overview copies —
+   than a patch release should make.
+   Only the disclosure is touched. Nothing here restyles the card, the type
+   scale or the color tokens; a full print stylesheet is out of scope for
+   v0.4.1.
+*/

+   COLOUR MECHANISM, in cascade order. shell.html emits three <style> blocks:

-/* ---- print -------------------------------------------------------------
-   The first and only @media print block in this stylesheet. It exists for
-   one reason (Q4): paper has no disclosure widget, so a printed viewer that
-   honoured the collapsed <details> would silently drop every claim's
-   governed_by/rests_on/implemented-in footer — the exact facts a reviewer
-   prints the page to read.
-   Revealing the contents through CSS is deliberate rather than setting `open`,
-   which CSS cannot do: `open` is a content attribute, not a property a rule
-   can write.
-   Same mechanism, and the same two-rule pairing, as the .claim:target rule
-   above: a closed <details> hides its contents through the UA's
-   ::details-content pseudo-element, so that is what is targeted, and the
-   child-selector form is expected to be a no-op wherever the pseudo-element is
-   implemented. It is kept only as a fallback for engines that predate
-   ::details-content (Chrome/Edge 131+, Safari 18.4+, Firefox 139+) and hide
-   the contents some other way; such an engine drops the pseudo-element rule
-   and still prints as it did before v0.4.1. Both rules declare the same value
-   and carry equal specificity (0,1,2), so the pseudo-element rule is written
-   LAST — source order is the only thing ranking them.
-   This block is independent of the .claim:target rule, of the two
-   server-written `open` signals, and of the expand-all toolbar — whichever of
-   those is or is not in effect on screen, print shows all four states
-   identically.
-   SCOPE — stated plainly so the next reader knows this is a decision, not an
-   oversight: only the facet currently ON SCREEN prints. A collapsed footer
-   belonging to a claim in a facet group the reader is not looking at stays
-   unrendered, because its ancestor section.claim-group carries the `hidden`
-   attribute (computed display: none) and no rule here un-hides it. The rules
-   below reveal a disclosure inside a subtree that is being laid out; they
-   cannot resurrect a subtree that display: none removed from the box tree in
-   the first place. That is deliberate: printing a tabbed viewer has always
-   shown one facet, what v0.4.1 changes is that the shown facet's footers now
-   print with it, and un-hiding every facet for print is a larger design
-   change — page order, per-facet headings, the duplicated overview copies —
-   than a patch release should make.

+/* ---- print — THE @media print block ------------------------------------
+   There is exactly one @media print block in this stylesheet and this is it;
+   internal/render/theme_tokens_test.go fails if a second one appears.
+
+   IT MUST STAY LAST IN THE FILE. Several of the rules below beat a screen
+   rule of identical specificity purely on source order — `.content-area
+   { padding: 0 }` against the padded `.content-area` rule in the System
+   Record layer, `.system-record-head { padding-top: 0 }` against that layer's
+   `.system-record-head`. Move this block earlier and the printed page silently
+   regains the sidebar gutter.
+
+   color-scheme is pinned to light here to match the palette: the :root at the
+   top of the file is light-first and its dark query is `screen`-scoped, so
+   print already gets light custom properties; this line makes the UA-painted
+   parts (form controls, scrollbars, canvas) agree. Unverified for Firefox and
+   Safari; where a browser already forces light for print it is a no-op, so it
+   is safe either way.
+
+   Consolidated from three separate @media print blocks. Their reasons follow,
+   unchanged, one per group.
+
+   NOTE (Q4): paper has no button to press, so the source-note clamp must not
+   reach it — print shows every note whole and hides the control.
+
+   DISCLOSURE (Q4). Paper has no disclosure widget, so a printed viewer that
+   honoured the collapsed <details> would silently drop every claim's
+   governed_by/rests_on/implemented-in footer — the exact facts a reviewer
+   prints the page to read.
+   Revealing the contents through CSS is deliberate rather than setting `open`,
+   which CSS cannot do: `open` is a content attribute, not a property a rule
+   can write.
+   Same mechanism, and the same two-rule pairing, as the .claim:target rule
+   above: a closed <details> hides its contents through the UA's
+   ::details-content pseudo-element, so that is what is targeted, and the
+   child-selector form is expected to be a no-op wherever the pseudo-element is
+   implemented. It is kept only as a fallback for engines that predate
+   ::details-content (Chrome/Edge 131+, Safari 18.4+, Firefox 139+) and hide
+   the contents some other way; such an engine drops the pseudo-element rule
+   and still prints as it did before v0.4.1. Both rules declare the same value
+   and carry equal specificity (0,1,2), so the pseudo-element rule is written
+   LAST — source order is the only thing ranking them.
+   This block is independent of the .claim:target rule, of the two
+   server-written `open` signals, and of the expand-all toolbar — whichever of
+   those is or is not in effect on screen, print shows all four states
+   identically.
+   SCOPE — stated plainly so the next reader knows this is a decision, not an
+   oversight: only the facet currently ON SCREEN prints. A collapsed footer
+   belonging to a claim in a facet group the reader is not looking at stays
+   unrendered, because its ancestor section.claim-group carries the `hidden`
+   attribute (computed display: none) and no rule here un-hides it. The rules
+   below reveal a disclosure inside a subtree that is being laid out; they
+   cannot resurrect a subtree that display: none removed from the box tree in
+   the first place. That is deliberate: printing a tabbed viewer has always
+   shown one facet, what v0.4.1 changes is that the shown facet's footers now
+   print with it, and un-hiding every facet for print is a larger design
+   change — page order, per-facet headings, the duplicated overview copies —
+   than a patch release should make.
+   Only the disclosure is touched. Nothing here restyles the card, the type
+   scale or the color tokens; a full print stylesheet is out of scope for
+   v0.4.1.
+*/
 @media print {
+  :root { color-scheme: light; }
+
+  /* source-note clamp */
+  .claim-source-note.is-clamped .claim-source-note-body {
+    display: block;
+    overflow: visible;
+  }
+
+  .claim-source-note-toggle {
+    display: none;
+  }
+
+  /* collapsed claim-links footer */
+  details.claim-links > *:not(summary) {
+    content-visibility: visible;
+  }
+
+  details.claim-links::details-content {
+    content-visibility: visible;
+  }
+
+  .claim-links-summary {
+    cursor: auto;
+  }
+
+  /* layout: chrome off the page, gutters closed */
   .system-record-head { padding-top: 0; }
   .sidebar,
   .nav-toggle,
